title: an-unbuildable-network-seal-refuses-the-run
intention: A proof whose network seal the tester cannot build is refused before it runs and nothing is persisted, so an unbuildable seal never lands in a record of truth as a RED verdict about the proof.
why: Measured 2026-10-06 under 72a37498c601: proofgate rewrote a crossing that named a proof as an argument into bin/cairn test --exec, and the cairn test --seal beside it ran nested. Inside --exec the instance seal inherits (c54d744aa9ac) but the network seal cannot: NetnsIsolation.available() says False (isolation.py:753-762), run_proof mints Seal('indeterminate') and runs the subject anyway (device.py:522-524), wrap() still emits bwrap --unshare-net, the subject dies 'bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace', and --seal persists that as the proof's RED (device.py:759-779). The record then says the proof failed when what failed was the harness — a false verdict in a record of truth (Law 7), and a red a peer leans on (Law 8). Inheriting is ruled out by measurement: inside --exec the route is open (connect to 1.1.1.1:443 succeeded, default route present, CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED unset, CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1). 68cef2ddd8ef routes verdict instruments through --exec, and any instrument that is itself cairn test --seal would land this false red. Measured at f5e53ec9 for clause (3): inside a real --exec the hollow already exited 2, but only after running test_proof_gate.py, whose bwrap died on the namespace and printed no tooth; on a bare host carrying the markers it measured at netns over an indeterminate seal and exited 0.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are permanent in records of truth, and a record of truth may not carry a false verdict: the harness failed, not the proof) and Law 8 (a false red persisted as a validation is a record a peer leans on); RULE 1 (the fix lives inside the tester, measured only there)
how: In TesterDevice.run_proof, where iso.seals_network and not iso.available() today mints Seal('indeterminate') and runs the subject anyway (wrap() still emits bwrap --unshare-net, which dies 'No permissions to create a new namespace'), raise a refusal (SealUnavailable, a ValueError beside SealDowngradeRefused) before anything runs or persists. cairn test catches it into its existing REFUSED lane (exit nonzero, nothing persisted, reason printed); the hollow turns it into HollowUnmeasurable (exit 2); the reseal door reports it as a refusal and seals nothing. Inheriting the outer seal is ruled out by measurement: inside bin/cairn test --exec the network is OPEN (2026-10-06, n=1: connect to 1.1.1.1:443 succeeded, default route present, CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED unset, CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1), so an inherited net seal would record sealed over an open route. The proof berths at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_an_unbuildable_network_seal_refuses_the_run.py: it builds a green fixture proof in a tmp dir and drives run_proof / bin/cairn test / --hollow in a subprocess whose env carries CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1 and lacks CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED, so no real nested namespace is needed and the live validation store is never written. Clause (4), folded 2026-10-06 at the peer's word: the --exec entry in cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json public_interface is reworded to say what --exec measured as — instance-sealed, network open — so no consumer (68cef2ddd8ef, 1af0564c0db3's rewrite) reads --exec as the full seal. The refusal's wording carries 'cannot be built' and 'not run', which the proof reads.
falsifier: RED if after the build: (1) run_proof(proof, sink='validations', isolation='netns') with CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED=1 and CAIRN_TESTER_SEALED unset in its environment runs the subject or writes a validation, instead of raising the refusal; (2) bin/cairn test --seal over that proof under the same markers exits 0, or prints no REFUSED line, or the proof's validation file changes; (3) bin/cairn test --hollow under the same markers measures a proof at netns instead of exiting 2 with a refusal that names the unbuildable seal before any proof runs (an exit 2 reached by running a proof into 'bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace' is measuring, not refusing); (4) the tester charter's public_interface entry for cairn test --exec does not say the run is instance-sealed with the network open. WRONG INTENT if the outer --exec wrap is measured to cut the network (then the seal should inherit, not refuse). Horizon: the tester seal of the new proof.

decisions.text: The proof already exists, committed red 5 of 5 at 34a8b36e: cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_an_unbuildable_network_seal_refuses_the_run.py, teeth named in its PROVES for this ticket (1 test_run_proof_refuses_before_the_subject_runs, 2 test_cairn_test_seal_refuses_and_persists_nothing, 3 test_the_hollow_exits_2_instead_of_measuring, 4 test_the_charter_says_exec_leaves_the_network_open) plus a composite. Do not rewrite it; build until it prints green 5 of 5 under bin/cairn test.

In cairn/devices/tester/device.py, module level: class SealUnavailable(ValueError), and a function refuse_unbuildable(iso) whose body is: available, why = iso.available(); if iso.seals_network and not available: raise SealUnavailable(f"cairn test: refused — the {iso.name} seal this proof asks for cannot be built here ({why}); the proof was not run"). The {why} in that f-string is the second value iso.available() returns (the reason string isolation.py already writes). The words 'cannot be built' and 'not run' are what tooth 1 reads.

In TesterDevice.run_proof, replace the branch 'if iso.seals_network and not available: seal = Seal("indeterminate", ...)' with a call to refuse_unbuildable(iso) placed right after iso = get_isolation(isolation), before any seal check, snapshot, run or persist; the else arm (seal = iso.check_seal(...)) becomes unconditional, and the now-unused 'available, why = iso.available()' line in run_proof goes. refuse_unbuildable is the module-level function of D2, defined in the same file (cairn/devices/tester/device.py) above class TesterDevice, so it is in scope when run_proof calls it.

In cairn/devices/tester/cli.py, import SealUnavailable from cairn.devices.tester.device and add a separate 'except SealUnavailable as refusal:' arm beside the existing (SealDowngradeRefused, SealConversionRefused) arm around tester.run_proof: print(f"  REFUSED {rel}  (not run: the seal it asks for cannot be built here)"), refused.append((proof, str(refusal))), continue. {rel} is the existing local rel = _rel(proof), assigned at the top of the same for-proof loop and already used by the neighbouring REFUSED print; it stays rel, not refusal. The existing exit 1 if (reds or refused) gives the nonzero exit.

HollowUnmeasurable is the existing RuntimeError class at cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py:132; cli.py's --hollow handler already prints it to stderr and returns 2. In measure(), right after depth = {rel: seal_isolation(repo_root / rel) for rel in proofs} (line 807; seal_isolation returns an isolation NAME string such as 'netns' or 'none', so depth.values() are strings) and before run_all() runs any proof: for name in sorted(set(depth.values())): try: refuse_unbuildable(get_isolation(name)) except SealUnavailable as e: raise HollowUnmeasurable(f"hollow: {e}") from e. get_isolation(name) is cairn.devices.tester.isolation.get_isolation and turns the name into the isolation instance refuse_unbuildable takes; import refuse_unbuildable and SealUnavailable from cairn.devices.tester.device inside measure(), beside its existing TesterDevice import.

Write the new tester charter via the artifact door, never by editing the file directly: (a) python3 reads cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json, replaces the one public_interface string containing '--exec' with exactly "cairn test --exec '<command>' [--timeout N]  (TesterDevice.run_exec: bash -c instance-sealed, network open — the instance seal only, no network seal; exit passes through, 2 when no seal)", and writes the whole JSON (indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, trailing newline) to a scratch file; (b) bin/cairn artifact write /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json --verb cast --why '67af8b743a63 clause 4' --from <that scratch file> — the first path is the record being replaced, --from is the new bytes; (c) run cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh.
